items.title: Randy Brecker interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, December 12, 2022
items.q: Coltrane was everyone’s idol... that all sunk in I suppose

ctx.x: Sort of back to the AHA moment question, I think you’ve actually answered it, but the creation of the Brecker Brothers and that intensity, was there a recording or a person that sort of inspired that? That made you head in that direction?

Well during those times that was kind of bashing — jam sessions, a lot of free music, Coltrane was everyone’s idol, and high intensity and playing was the hors d’oeuvres so to speak of the day. So in the early 60s that all sunk in I suppose and of course when Mike discovered Coltrane that was it for him. And I was in the throes, when I first moved to New York, of the Brecker-Liebman-Bob Berg-Steve Grossman complex where they played together quite a bit. And I was in on that so I was around a lot of tenor players,…
Would that include James Brown? © Fillius Jazz Archive -8-
